reasons.text: Energy charges do not match units x tariff on 100% of bills (worst bill charged 18% of expected)
Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 181% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
54% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Declared capacity of 23,690 t/yr needs about 2.5x the power the plant is connected for
23% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
68% of certificate tonnes were generated more than 45 days after the processing month

inspection_checklist: Verify the electricity bills directly with the DISCOM (units, tariff, amount); the uploaded copies do not reconcile.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
